NFL DFS Tight End Rankings: Week 11 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, November 22 · 10 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of November 19, 11:20 AM ET

Trey McBride is the top-projected tight end on the Week 11 DraftKings main slate at 13.6 DraftKings points for $6,600, at Kansas City. Isaiah Likely (13.4, $5,600) and Colston Loveland (13.3, $5,100) are next.

Colston Loveland returns the most per dollar among tight ends projected for at least 7 points: 2.61 projected points per $1,000 at $5,100.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the November 19, 11:20 AM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Tight ends to know in Week 11

Trey McBride, ARI at KC ($6,600)

Trey McBride carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 13.6 DraftKings points at $6,600. That is 0.2 points clear of Isaiah Likely. The model gives him 11.9 targets on 34.8 routes. The salary works out to 2.06 projected points per $1,000, 11th of 13 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations McBride averaged 13.7 points with a simulated floor of 2.5 and a ceiling of 35.5, and he holds 5% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Arizona is a 15.5-point underdog on the road against Kansas City, with an implied team total of 12.5 in a game totaled at 40.5.

Isaiah Likely, NYG vs JAX ($5,600)

Isaiah Likely projects 2nd at the position with 13.4 DraftKings points at $5,600. The model gives him 7.4 targets on 28.6 routes. The salary works out to 2.40 projected points per $1,000, 5th of 13 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Likely averaged 13.4 points with a simulated floor of 2.3 and a ceiling of 35.7, and he holds 11% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. The Giants are a 6-point underdog at home against Jacksonville, with an implied team total of 20.25 in a game totaled at 46.5.

Value: Mark Andrews, BAL at CAR ($3,500)

Mark Andrews projects for 8.8 DraftKings points at $3,500, which works out to 2.52 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 13 tight ends the model projects for 7 or more points. The model gives him 4.6 targets on 20.1 routes. Across 10,000 simulations Andrews averaged 8.9 points with a simulated floor of 0.0 and a ceiling of 31.5, and he holds 12% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Baltimore is a 2.5-point underdog on the road against Carolina, with an implied team total of 20.5 in a game totaled at 43.5.
